text: The masking_rule rows for DF-ACE-281 at the masking version in force carry unmasked true for RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-SPECIAL and RW-GUARANT, and unmasked false for RW-PHONECOL and every other role that holds Case record R.
why: The legacy story states this roster and marks it 'assumed; DL26'; no FSD, TSD or BRD row fixes it and masking_rule carries no seed rows.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-003 sections 3 and 10; FSD P4 A2.5; TSD P4 T3.1 masking_rule; Architecture v5 slide 41 (P4 owns the masking policy).
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer (RW-COMPLY), through the masking load path of RWB-P4-AD004-APP
impact: A missing clear row masks a role that should see the number; an extra clear row exposes a number to a role that should not see it.

text: The masking version of the wave-2 release is MASK-2026.12, and the version in force for a business date is the one whose valid_from is the latest on or before that date.
why: masking_rule is versioned by masking_version with valid_from and valid_to, but no source names the version in force at the release date or the rule for a day with two valid versions.
read: TSD P4 T3.1 (DF-REF-202 to DF-REF-204); FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-004-05 (MASK-SIT-01 example); Architecture v5 slide 14.
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer (RW-COMPLY) and the solution architect
impact: A wrong label misnames the version in every answer; a wrong selection rule answers under a superseded roster for a day.

text: DF-ACE-281 (v_ace_party_product.account_no) is the only personal field of the other-products panel that this service masks; the other six fields of the view carry no masking row and are named as identifiers only.
why: Legacy section 11 lists the seven fields the panel reads and names a masking row for account_no only; neither the FSD field catalogues nor TSD P4 T3.1 carry a personal-data classification for the ACE view.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-003 section 11; FSD P4 A2.5; TSD P4 T3.1; DL26.
confirm: Data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW), in the data dictionary
impact: If a second field is personal, the panel shows it unmasked; if a classification is wrong, an extra row masks a field that never needed it.

text: The gateway-bff composite route for SCR-03 carries one row per product with the masked or clear account-number string this answer names, and applies no masking rule of its own.
why: DP-19 gives the panel a composite route, but no source gives the route's field list, its merge order or where the last-four shape is applied.
read: Architecture v5 slide 20 and DP-19; legacy RWB-E2-003 section 15; FSD P4 Screens.
confirm: Solution architect, with the gateway-bff route story under RWB-PLT-N001-CON
impact: A route that masks on its own can disagree with the answer; a route that carries the value clear defeats the answer.

text: The PII access event of the other-products read is written once by rwb-integration through ACE Common on INT-22; rwb-access writes no decision record, no audit entry and no event for this capability.
why: The legacy story writes the event inside its reader, and the composed read has two candidate writers; Architecture v5 gives audit and PII logging to ACE Common, and DP-03 and DP-09 are not patterns of this story.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-003 section 4 step 8 and BR5; TSD P4 T5.1 (INT-22); Architecture v5 slide 13 note and slide 14 (P4 events: the two policy events only).
confirm: Solution architect, with rwb-integration (RWB-P2-E2003-APP) and the ACE Common owner
impact: Two writers duplicate every event; no writer leaves the read unlogged.

text: The masking answer is a record per field ID holding the field ID, the marker clear or masked, the last-four shape where masked, and the masking version used; its field names are the ones RWB-P4-E1037-CON publishes.
why: TSD P4 T-A.1 gives no schema for the masking read and slide 14 describes /authorise only in prose, so the names of the answer's fields are not fixed anywhere.
read: TSD P4 Appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; Architecture v5 slide 14; legacy RWB-E2-003 section 12 (Masking.apply).
confirm: Solution architect, in the published contract RWB-P4-E1037-CON
impact: A name mismatch breaks the contract test between this answer and every caller of /authorise and /masking-policies.

text: The database login of rwb-access carries its own name and is not the shared recovery_svc login; this story refers to it as the rwb-access login (DP-02) and names no login string.
why: DP-02 gives one login per service and Architecture v5 slide 41 gives each schema its own login, but no source fixes the name of this service's login.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-02; Architecture v5 slide 41 and slide 20; TSD P4 T1; DP-01 and DP-02.
confirm: ACE database administrator, in the platform DB story
impact: A shared login would let one service read another schema; a missing login blocks the migration and every read of the service.
